name: Gangrel of Note (Wolves at the Door Lore)

text.content:
Matasuntha came out of the East with the first Hunnic horde in the latter half of the fourth century and swiftly dominated the Gangrel of the West. In 400 CE she summoned a Grand Gather and defeated every challenger, and the clan named her queen and called her the Hun. For a decade she led the Gangrel in a Grand Revel that swept across Europe, always found wherever the destruction was greatest — a powerful, ancient figure with tiger-striped fur, yellow eyes and long talons. Then, as suddenly as she had risen, she vanished.

For five hundred years nothing was heard of her. In the early 900s she reappeared in the Alps, more tiger than woman and much subdued, apparently starved from her long absence; many Cainites disappeared from Italy and Germany in the years following her return. Those few who survived an encounter and lived to tell of it say she spoke of a battle with a Cainite in the catacombs beneath Rome, and of long years spent afterward in torpor. In recent nights the Hun is returning to her old strength, her wounds and hunger sated, and she is said to be seeking out Gangrel across the Holy Roman Empire, speaking to them of a Grand Gather she means to call soon — though she now finds competition for the clan's attention in the North, where the self-proclaimed All-High holds sway, and many younger Gangrel no longer remember or heed the glory of which she speaks.

Yesugei — known to the Franks as Oderic — claims to be the most-traveled Gangrel alive, a wanderer who was old before the coming of Rome and older still when he watched it fall. He carries news and stories of the clan from corner to corner of the known world, weaving together the scattered Gathers of Europe, Scandinavia, Iberia, the Balkans and the Holy Land into something resembling a shared clan consciousness. He counts the Lupines he has survived on both hands and those he has killed on a single claw, and he freely admits Clan Gangrel is more numerous than any Cainite suspects — a fact he considers the clan's greatest ongoing advantage, since the city-bound clans never think to count.

Yesugei serves the clan less as a leader than as a living archive and messenger, a role that makes him welcome (if rarely fully trusted) at nearly any Gather he chooses to attend. His travels have given him an unusually broad view of Gangrel society across the Dark Medieval world, from the civilized affectations of the Norman Gangrel of England to the scholar-warriors of Taifa Iberia and the reclusive Gangrel enclaves rumored to be forming in Constantinople and Paris.

Rimantas, named "Road" in seven tongues, is an elder who witnessed the fall of Rome, defended the Pripet Marshes against incursion, and claims to have taken the head of a Giant of the East in single combat. In recent nights he has taken it upon himself to mentor newly accepted childer of the clan, teaching them the traditions of the Gather, the rites of status, and the clan's version of its own history — the tale of Ennoia, Churka and the Betrayal that split the Gangrel from the Ravnos in the deep past.

Rimantas represents a strand of Gangrel elder who takes the clan's oral traditions seriously as a survival tool: he holds that a childe who understands her place in the long war against the Ravnos and the Giants of the East, and who knows the customs that bind Gangrel loosely together, is measurably more likely to survive her first century than one left to guess at the rules of a society that leaves almost nothing in writing.

Bodhmall is one of the Gangrel elders who has claimed the Welsh Marches as her territory, part of a small circle of clanmates in the region with a well-earned reputation for hungering after Cainite blood over that of mere mortals. Unusually for a Gangrel of her ferocity, she has maintained an ongoing, wary line of communication with the local Lupines, who she reports are willing to talk rather than immediately fight — a claim that most Gangrel elsewhere in Europe dismiss as either a lie or an aberration specific to Wales.

Whether Bodhmall's arrangement with the Lupines constitutes a genuine truce or merely a longer-than-usual cessation of hostilities is a matter of dispute even among the Gangrel who know of it, but it has made Wales a subject of curiosity for travelers of the clan — and a place most are still wise enough to approach with extreme caution, given both the elder Gangrel already prowling its hills and the packs of Lupines that guard them.

vtmlarp.source: Libellus Sanguinis III: Wolves at the Door, Book One: Animals
